reasoning_traces.think:
The core mechanism involves afferent interaction between stimulus components within a compound, modifying their effective habit strengths. Initially, a compound S1+S2 yields 40.95 habs, but due to afferent interaction, each component's contribution is altered. When presented individually, S1 produces a weaker reaction than expected because its effective habit strength has been diminished by interaction with S2. This modulation is governed by a generalized stimulus generalization gradient, where the effective habit strength of a component depends on the intensity of afferent interaction during conditioning. The failure mode occurs when interaction is strong enough to reduce a component’s effective habit strength below half of the original compound value, resulting in overshadowing. This leads to a breakdown in predictive accuracy of individual stimulus effects, necessitating a probabilistic model of habit strength distribution across components.
